title: QuantumLoom marketplace listing & joint-solution architecture sync
summary: Architectural alignment for QuantumLoom's upcoming marketplace listing and joint-solution packaging. Discussed marketplace packaging options (helm vs operator), VPC/KMS requirements, private deployment compatibility, telemetry and canary rollout strategy, and a performance pilot to validate latency/cost tradeoffs. Actionable next steps and owners captured.
topics: Marketplace packaging: Helm chart, OCI bundle, operator
Reference architecture for hybrid deployments (VPC + on-prem connector)
Quantization and model variant routing for cost/latency
Pilot plan: test dataset, perf targets, timeline
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-02 15:00 UTC | Duration 62m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Elena (CTO), Markus (Head of Cloud), Sanjay (DevOps)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call — hi Elena, hi Markus, Sanjay — can you hear us okay?
[00:12] Elena: Yep yeah, loud and clear. Thanks Maya. Excited to go through the listing flow and the joint-solution runbook.
[00:18] Liam: Hi team, Liam from Redwood. I'll drive the technical bits. We prepared an initial reference diagram, shared in the invite (link: https://redwood.app/quantumloom/refarch).
[00:29] Markus: Got it, we pulled the doc. A couple things up front — QuantumLoom needs a marketplace listing in AWS marketplace and GCP marketplace, and an on-prem-friendly packaging for customers that cannot use cloud-hosted endpoints.
[00:43] Maya: Great. We'll cover packaging options and then dive into the hybrid reference arch, including VPC peering, private control plane options, and KMS integration.
[00:55] Sanjay: Important note: our security team requires CMEK + HSM-backed keys and audit hooks into our SIEM. Also need RBAC syncing with our IdP (SAML).
[01:07] Liam: Understood. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM via our KMS connector and audit log plugin. There are a few implementation variants — we can either host the control plane in your VPC or run a customer-managed control plane on-prem.
[01:24] Elena: For enterprise customers we want the control plane in their VPC. Can the listing artifact still be a marketplace product?
[01:33] Liam: Yes — marketplace listing is compatible; the product asset can be an installer (OCI bundle) or a Terraform module that sets up the VPC attachments and the private control plane. The marketplace listing just points to the installer/URL.
[01:47] Markus: Ok, what about packaging — helm chart vs operator vs simple container? We've seen other vendors push operators which are heavy.
[01:57] Liam: Good question. Helm chart + OCI bundle is the lightest path and easiest for marketplace packaging. Operator is useful if you need lifecycle hooks across many clusters, but it's more overhead for customers. Our recommendation: Helm for initial listing, provide an operator as an advanced option in the joint-solution repo.
[02:18] Elena: Makes sense. How do we handle quantization recommendations? We expect customers to want smaller models for cost reasons.
[02:27] Liam: We can supply recommended model variants and quantization profiles in the reference architecture — e.g., int8 profiles for latency-sensitive endpoints, float16 for higher quality. Redwood Optimize will surface those suggestions based on workload traces. We'll include an example config in the repo.
[02:44] Sanjay: Are there compatibility concerns with on-prem GPUs — e.g., A100 vs T4?
[02:50] Liam: There are performance differences. We'll include a kernel/compat matrix and an automated benchmark playbook. For on-prem we'll suggest supported drivers and a fallback to CPU for non-GPU nodes with clear SLO degradation notes.
[03:05] Maya: I want to flag the telemetry requirements — QuantumLoom asked for per-route latency and token-cost breakdowns in the console. Can we expose that?
[03:14] Liam: Yes, Redwood Console supports per-model and per-route telemetry; we can add a pre-made dashboard in the joint-solution repo. We can also instrument traces to push to your SIEM via OpenTelemetry.
[03:26] Markus: What about canary and rollout behavior when releasing a new model? We need automatic fallback to a smaller variant under congestion.
[03:34] Liam: We support canary rollouts with traffic weights and automated fallback policies. You can configure routing policies by latency SLO or cost thresholds; the control plane will route to a compatible variant when primary is overloaded. We'll include sample policies in the repo.
[03:50] Elena: Security — SOC2/ISO documentation, audit logs, SSO. We'll need a security pack to send to procurement.
[04:00] Maya: We'll send the security pack and SOC2 report after the call. Also include SSO/SAML integration guide and the runbook for audit log ingestion.
[04:09] Sanjay: One thing — data residency. Some customers require EU-only processing. How do we set region pinning in the marketplace listing?
[04:18] Liam: Region pinning is a deployment artifact: the installer can enforce deployment to specific regions and the marketplace listing can include region availability. For Redwood Hosted, we'll ensure routing to EU regions for those customers.
[04:31] Maya: Let's talk pilot plan. We propose a two-week perf pilot with a representative dataset, measuring p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, and memory usage. Does that align with your expectations?
[04:45] Elena: Yes. Pilot success criteria: p95 under 350ms for chat endpoints, and cost within 20% of our target. We'll provide sample workload and tooling.
[04:56] Liam: We'll run a lab with quantized and non-quantized variants, show tradeoffs, and produce a benchmark spreadsheet.
[05:06] Markus: Timeline — we need listing live in marketplace by Q3. Can Redwood commit to a packaging + review cadence?
[05:14] Maya: Yes. Proposed: 2 weeks to finalize packaging, 3 weeks for integration and security review, 2 weeks for marketplace listing & approval cycles. We'll iterate.
[05:26] Sanjay: Integration questions — do we need a VPN or can we use private link?
[05:31] Liam: Both are supported. PrivateLink/Private Service Connect is recommended for lower ops overhead. We'll include deployment patterns for both.
[05:40] Elena: Anything we should flag for enterprise customers who want air-gapped installs?
[05:45] Liam: For air-gapped, we'll provide an on-prem installer tarball and offline licensing keys; that will require a little more manual installation and an operator can help with lifecycle.
[05:58] Maya: Okay going deeper — can we walk through the reference diagram? (screen share)
[06:04] Liam: On the diagram, left is customer VPC with private subnets, middle is the Redwood private control plane in the customer VPC, right is optional on-prem connector. The model artifacts are stored in an OCI registry and model variant routing happens at the control plane. Prefix caching is optional for hot endpoints.
[06:28] Markus: On caching — how does KV cache work across scale? We have many short chat sessions.
[06:34] Liam: Redwood supports distributed KV cache that can be colocated with the inference nodes; we have TTLs and warm-up strategies. We'll provide recommended TTLs and cache sizing examples.
[06:46] Elena: For compliance, we also need immutable audit logs for model access. Is that part of the audit plugin?
[06:54] Liam: Yes, the audit plugin writes immutable events to your logging backend with HMAC signatures; we can also forward to your SIEM.
[07:02] Sanjay: A couple of nitty-gritty: helm values for KMS config — do you accept keys as ARNs or do we require a secrets manager?
[07:11] Liam: Both. The helm values accept either KMS ARNs or references to a secrets manager. For HSM-backed keys there's a small connector that we install as a sidecar for the control plane.
[07:24] Maya: Let's capture dependencies for marketplace approval — packaging, security pack, test plan, legal agreements, and a go-to-market blurb. We'll own the marketplace asset, you (QuantumLoom) will own the go-to-market blurb and pricing guidance.
[07:39] Elena: Pricing — we want a joint pricing model ideally with per-1k token pass-through plus a managed service surcharge. Can you provide a draft?
[07:48] Maya: We'll share a draft by EOD Thursday. It will include hosted and dedicated options and an example TCO calculation.
[07:57] Markus: On telemetry again — can we get per-tenant cost visibility? We run multi-tenant customers and need chargeback.
[08:05] Liam: Yes, we have token-level attribution and can export cost per tenant via our billing API. We'll include an example export.
[08:16] Elena: Any blockers for starting the pilot?
[08:19] Liam: We need access to a representative workload, kube cluster credentials for the lab, and a list of model artifacts to test. Also a signed pilot NDA.
[08:30] Sanjay: We'll prepare that. Timeline — can we start lab runs next week?
[08:34] Maya: Tentatively yes; we'll schedule the kickoff once we have the NDA and the test dataset.
[08:40] Elena: Ok, let's open to Q&A.
[08:42] Markus: On marketplace approvals, we've seen long approval times on GCP. Any tips?
[08:47] Maya: For GCP, pre-submit the security pack and use the marketplace sandbox to validate the installer. We'll provide a submission checklist.
[08:56] Sanjay: About the operator path — if we don't want operator day-one, what's the upgrade story?
[09:01] Liam: The helm chart supports in-place upgrades. Operator makes orchestration of multiple clusters easier later. We'll document migration steps.
[09:12] Elena: Great. Anything else?
[09:15] Maya: Quick recap and next steps in a bit, but first — competitors. Have you evaluated others?
[09:21] Elena: We looked at NorthStar.AI and HelioGrid. They had tighter marketplace packaging but not the hybrid control plane we're after.
[09:31] Liam: Good to know. We'll highlight the hybrid offering in the joint-solution repo.
[09:36] Maya: Alright, recap: we'll send security pack, draft pricing, packaging checklist, and the pilot NDA. Action items assigned.
[09:46] Elena: Thanks everyone.
[09:48] Markus: Thanks.
[09:49] Sanjay: Thanks.
[09:50] Maya: End of recording.

Note: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., 'operator' sometimes transcribed as 'opertor'), filler words preserved.
